key_insight: MeanFlowNFT extends forward-process RL to MeanFlow-style generators, enabling alignment and optimization without needing reverse-process trajectories or likelihood estimation. This makes it possible to improve fast average-velocity generation while keeping sampling efficient.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to apply reinforcement learning-based alignment methods to MeanFlow generators, which predict average velocities rather than standard reverse-diffusion steps. Existing RL approaches like DiffusionNFT do not directly transfer to this setting.
method: Adapts forward-process reinforcement learning to average-velocity generators instead of reverse-process diffusion models.
Uses optimization signals that avoid likelihood estimation and reverse trajectory reconstruction.
Targets efficient few-step generation while improving alignment with task-specific objectives or preferences.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it brings RL-based control and alignment to a class of fast generative models that are attractive for low-latency deployment. It can help make efficient generators more adaptable to human feedback and downstream requirements.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing MeanFlow generation versus forward-process RL flow.
A side-by-side comparison of diffusion, DiffusionNFT, and MeanFlowNFT.

A before/after chart showing improved alignment or preference scores with few-step sampling.
paper_title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators
paper_authors: Yushi Huang, Xiangxin Zhou, Jun Zhang, Liefeng Bo, Tianyu Pang
